environment.description: Container deployed on a Kubernetes pod with a custom seccomp profile loaded via the node's /var/lib/kubelet/seccomp/profiles/tf-provider-hardened.json. The profile operates in defaultAction SCMP_ACT_ERRNO mode with an explicit allowlist. The allowed syscalls include read, write, close, fstat, mmap, mprotect, munmap, brk, rt_sigaction, rt_sigprocmask, ioctl, access, pipe, select, sched_yield, mremap, msync, mincore, madvise, shmget, shmat, shmctl, dup, dup2, pause, nanosleep, getitimer, alarm, setitimer, getpid, sendfile, connect (AF_UNIX only via BPF filter), accept, recvfrom, sendto (AF_UNIX only), bind, listen, getsockname, getpeername, clone, fork, vfork, exit, wait4, kill, uname, fcntl, flock, fsync, fdatasync, truncate, ftruncate, getdents, getcwd, chdir, rename, mkdir, rmdir, link, unlink, chmod, chown, lstat, stat, readlink, epoll_create, epoll_ctl, epoll_wait, openat, newfstatat, set_robust_list, futex, clock_gettime, epoll_create1, pipe2, eventfd2, accept4, timerfd_create, timerfd_settime, getrandom, memfd_create, copy_file_range. Notably ABSENT from the allowlist: execve, execveat, ptrace, socket (the connect/sendto entries use pre-existing AF_UNIX file descriptors inherited from the container runtime shim, not new socket creation). The pod also has a NetworkPolicy restricting egress to only the Kubernetes DNS service (UDP/53) and the Terraform state backend (TCP/443 to a specific CIDR). The container runs as UID 65534 (nobody) with readOnlyRootFilesystem: true and allowPrivilegeEscalation: false.

config.network_policy: egress only to kube-dns:53/UDP and state-backend:443/TCP
